# E0509: row variable on a parameter that passes its effects through

A function parameter passes the effects its row doesn't name through to the caller, so a row variable adds nothing. Delete it, or mark the parameter `escaping` if the function keeps it.

- Rule: [`effects.row-variables`](../../reference/12-effects.md#effects.row-variables)
- Reported at: the first row variable written in the parameter's type.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0509:1
fn apply<e>(x: i64, f: fn(i64) -> i64 / e) -> i64 / e { f(x) }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn apply(x: i64, f: fn(i64) -> i64) -> i64 { f(x) }
```

```text
  1 │ fn apply<e>(x: i64, f: fn(i64) -> i64 / e) -> i64 / e { f(x) }

A function parameter passes the effects its row doesn't name through to the
caller, so a row variable adds nothing. Delete it, or mark the parameter
`escaping` if the function keeps it.

Two ways to fix it:

  1. Delete `e` from the signature:

  1 │ fn apply<e>(x: i64, f: fn(i64) -> i64 / e) -> i64 / e { f(x) }
    │         ---                          ----        ----

  2. Mark `f` `escaping`, if the function keeps it:

  1 │ fn apply<e>(x: i64, escaping f: fn(i64) -> i64 / e) -> i64 / e { f(x) }
    │                     +++++++++
```

```text
A function parameter passes the effects its row doesn't name through to the
caller, so a row variable adds nothing. Delete it, or mark the parameter
`escaping` if the function keeps it.

To fix it, mark `f` `escaping`, if the function keeps it:

  1 │ fn compose<e>(escaping f: fn(i64) -> i64 / e, escaping g: fn(i64) -> i64 / e) -> fn(i64) -> i64 / e {
    │               +++++++++
```
